AT-003.reason: Round 1, unchanged. The audio lanes no longer override _drop_queued_tasks, so request_stop(graceful=False) only sets the halt flag. Queued rows are claimed just in time, and request_start resumes the drain.

AT-008.reason: r1 verified. orch_generate.request_cancel, after a successful _generation_jobs.cancel, calls orch_resources.wake_owner and orch_sources.wake_sentence_waiters(task). For book tasks that calls orch_books.wake_sentence_waiters -> _sync_jobs.notify(source_key), which sets job_signal(source_key). ensure_book_sentences clears the signal, checks cancel_requested(), then waits on the signal. A cancel that lands after the check leaves the signal set, so the wait returns at once and no wakeup is lost. Text tasks skip the call (is_text_task).

AT-034.reason: r1 verified; the round 1 blocker is resolved. The retained file is <app cache>/qwen_operations/f'{operation_id}_{item.id}.{audio_format}' (operation_service.py:165). Both ids come from pyutils/common/operation_service: op_ is f'op_{uuid4().hex}' at line 101, and item_ is f'item_{uuid4().hex}' at line 262. item_key is used only for the bus client_job_id and never reaches a path. audio_format goes through normalize_audio_format (allow-list wav/mp3, default wav). It is checked at the RPC entry (ui_service.synthesis_submit rejects the value with unsupported_format before create_or_get, and the only caller of submit is ui_service) and again in _run. _retained_audio_path resolves the path and refuses it unless its parent equals the resolved qwen_operations dir. A write or guard failure fails the item and the operation (audio_store_failed) instead of leaving the item running. The skip that prevents a re-run is unchanged. Scratch run with the same logic: '../x', 'wav/../../y', 'ogg' and 'wav\x00' are rejected; 'MP3' becomes mp3; ''/None become wav; 'a/../../b' and 'x/y' as an id are refused. No UI caller of qwenSynthesisSubmit exists (only the route constant in PycoreHttpRoutes.ts:279), so the allow-list breaks no client.

issues: (non-blocking, AT-036 follow-up) pycore/pyutils/tts/memory_gate.py:147 _gpu_query (used by gpu_stats and the memory gate) still calls nvidia-smi through exec_silent without a timeout. pycore/pyfoundations/third_party/_torch_cuda.py:132 uses a literal timeout=15. So the report's claim that the constant is 'the single bound for every nvidia-smi call in pycore' is not accurate. Both sites are outside the AT-036 finding (the two servers). Fix: pass timeout=NVIDIA_SMI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS in _gpu_query (and in _torch_cuda), and correct the report sentence.

(non-blocking, AT-034) submit treats only 'running' items as in flight (ITEM_ACTIVE_STATUSES). An idempotent re-submit that arrives after start_bus_task but before _run's start_item starts a second _run for the same item. The window is small (thread start), and the round 1 behaviour is unchanged. Consider treating a queued item whose worker was just scheduled as in flight.
